rule.question: How does PokéDate find my Pokémon?
rule.answer: We take the last digit of the day, the month and the year of your date and put them side by side. 17/10/2026 gives 7, 0 and 6: that's Pokémon no. 706, Goodra. If all three digits are 0, you get no. 1000.

birthday.question: Which Pokémon am I based on my birth date?
birthday.answer: Enter your birthday in the form at the top of the page: your Pokémon shows up with its types, stats, weaknesses and evolutions. Someone born on the same day as you but in another year usually gets another Pokémon: the last digit of the year changes everything.

shiny.question: What is a shiny Pokémon?
shiny.answer: It's a version with rare colours. About one date in twenty gives a shiny Pokémon, and it's always the same for a given date: see if yours is one of them.

bonus.question: How do I find Pokémon no. 1001 to 1025?
bonus.answer: They don't come out with the usual rule. You need a “mirror date”, where the day and the month are the same (01/01, 02/02… 12/12): one of these rare Pokémon then appears as a bonus.

privacy.question: Is my data stored?
privacy.answer: There's no account, no cookie and no tracker. Your Pokédex is stored only in your browser, and the links you share never contain your birth date. When you reveal your Pokémon, it's added to the latest draws with your nickname (or “Anonymous”) and the time, visible to everyone for 7 days at most, never with your date. You can remove it or turn this off from its card.

legal.title: Legal notice
legal.seoDescription: Publisher, host, intellectual property and personal data of PokéDate.
legal.publisher: PokéDate is a personal, non-commercial project published by Quentin Macq in a private capacity. Contact: {contact}.
legal.hostAddress: 101 Townsend St, San Francisco, CA 94107, United States
legal.ipTrademarks: Pokémon and the related names, images and sounds are trademarks and works of Nintendo, Game Freak and The Pokémon Company. PokéDate is a fan project, unaffiliated with these companies and non-commercial.
legal.ipSources: Data and images come from {pokeapi}. The French Pokédex descriptions of the most recent Pokémon (no. 899 to 1025) come from {pokepedia}, under the {licence} licence.
legal.ipRequests: For any request about some content, write to the publisher: it will be removed quickly if needed.
legal.dataAccount: PokéDate doesn't ask for any account.
legal.dataDraws: When you reveal your Pokémon from a date, PokéDate adds it to the latest draws: it stores your nickname (or “Anonymous”), the Pokémon's number and the time, 5 draws a day at most. They're shown publicly on the latest draws page (the 50 most recent) and deleted after 7 days at most. You can remove a draw or turn off adding them from the Pokémon's card. Neither your date nor your IP address is stored; the IP address is only used, at that moment, to limit the number of publications.
legal.dataDates: The dates you enter are only used to work out your Pokémon. The links you share never contain your birth date, only the Pokémon's number.
legal.dataPokedex: Your Pokédex is stored in your browser (local storage) and never leaves your device. You can erase it by deleting the site's data in your browser.
legal.dataAnalytics: No cookie, no advertising tracker. Visits are counted by {analytics}, which sets no cookie, stores nothing on your device and keeps neither your IP address nor URL parameters (so never your date). Only overall statistics come out of it: page views, country, device type, referring site. Fonts, images and sounds are served by the site itself.
legal.dataCounts: PokéDate also counts, day by day, the total number of some actions (Pokémon revealed, duels, tournaments, shares…) and how many times each Pokémon is drawn, with nothing that could tell who did them. To count neither your visits nor your actions, open {optOut} once on each device.
legal.dataNoAnalytics: No cookie, no audience measurement, no advertising tracker. Fonts, images and sounds are served by the site itself, without calling any third-party service.
legal.dataLogs: The host keeps technical logs in case of errors, without the full address of the pages visited.
